ocelhq-9d3.oneLine: AWS Lambda ConcurrentExecutions quota is 10; bursts throttle and surface as 502

matchers.check: Throttle iff the response carries no x-amzn-requestid AND CloudWatch shows no START RequestId for the function. Otherwise it is a real origin error.

matchers.pattern: semantically wrong 200 (redirect that does not redirect, notFound() returning 200, handler headers absent) with NO throttle marker
matchers.check: MANDATORY re-run solo before spawning any debugger. Quota contention also corrupts responses silently: the request reaches Lambda, returns 200 and carries x-amzn-requestid, so the "no x-amzn-* AND no CloudWatch START" rule correctly declines to call it a throttle. The only signal is latency - affected requests are ~2x slower than their own neighbours in the same run. Confirmed iff the failures vanish on a solo re-run with no source change.

ocelhq-9d3.note: Two failure modes. (1) Loud: 429 TooManyRequestsException, or a Cloudflare-generated 502 with no x-amzn-* headers. (2) Silent, characterised in sweep-2026-07-27b: semantically wrong 200s with no throttle marker of any kind - see the closed ocelhq-nbk for the controlled proof. Mode 2 is indistinguishable from a genuine adapter defect on response evidence alone and cost a full debugger budget. Calibration: 16 concurrent GETs return 429s that DO carry x-amzn-requestid, so a 429 proves throttling but its absence proves nothing. Operationally: SUITES_PER_WAVE must be 1 until this quota is raised. sweep-2026-07-27g, NEW DATA from the ocelhq-slzm triage: the idle-gap 502 was reproduced on two independent previews (first POST after a 25-35s idle gap), and the Lambda IS invoked — 2.25ms and 2.47ms with no output. Reinforces that this is the worker->Function-URL response leg, not throttling. Retitle recommended.
ocelhq-9d3.closeNote: Premise dead: quota is 1000. 11/16 attributed tests recovered unchanged; the other 5 were misattributions, re-homed to ocelhq-dan, ocelhq-qcpc and ocelhq-r6ul. Non-throttle 502 evidence carried forward by ocelhq-r6ul.

ocelhq-e7w.oneLine: Pages-router prerendered HTML written to static/ without .html: EEXIST kills `ocel build` outright, and served as application/octet-stream
ocelhq-e7w.fixSite: next-adapter.mts:233-241 (the mkdir on :239 is what throws)
ocelhq-e7w.note: RAISED P2 -> P0 in sweep-2026-07-27c. Two faces, one defect. (1) Response-time: served as octet-stream, 'Download is starting'. (2) BUILD-TIME: stripping the extension makes a pages-router prerender at /x occupy the FILE name static/x, which is the DIRECTORY name any static output under /x/ needs; mkdir(recursive:true) tolerates an existing dir but throws EEXIST on an existing file. Verified the .html fix alone resolves it against a 5-file synthetic app; no separate collision guard needed. Ordering is irrelevant - child-first makes mkdir create static/x as a directory and the parent's copyFile then fails EISDIR. AFFECTS REAL APPS: pages/blog.js + pages/blog/[slug].js is ordinary routing; with an app/ dir present even a getStaticProps child triggers it via the .rsc fallback static file. Blast radius: blocks app-dir/app (and its 4 sibling suites experimental-compile, useReportWebVitals, standalone, standalone-gsp), app-dir/hooks, e2e/dynamic-routing, e2e/index-index. Ruled out: custom-routes, switchable-runtime, basepath, prerender, telemetry.

ocelhq-sae.oneLine: Static metadata assets stamped with Go mime.TypeByExtension at upload; immutable cache-control applied unconditionally
ocelhq-sae.overMatchWarning: Its route matcher covers /robots.txt, which caused a Cloudflare Managed-robots.txt environment artifact to be auto-attributed here in sweep-2026-07-27b. Before attributing a /robots.txt failure to this issue, confirm the defect is content-type/cache-control AND that the body carries no Cloudflare Managed content. AMENDED in sweep-2026-07-27c: the Managed transform also STRIPS cache-control, so a null cache-control on /robots.txt is the zone artifact, not sae - the previous wording ('the defect is content-type/cache-control') actively misroutes that case. serveStaticAsset sets cache-control unconditionally, so an ABSENT cache-control can never have come from the asset path at all.

ocelhq-e8z.oneLine: next.config.js redirects 404 with a correct Location header (processRoutes guards on a destination Next never sets)

matchers.pattern: any non-3xx response carrying a location header
matchers.check: Broadened in sweep-2026-07-27b. The status is DATA-DEPENDENT on whether a prerender exists under the slash-free key: /a and /metadata give 200+location (prerender exists), /en and /nope give 404+location (none). The old matcher said "404 with a location header present", which could not match the 200-face at all - that gap cost a full debugging budget when a runner concluded the mechanisms differed.

CONFIRMED in sweep-2026-07-27b, not refuted. A runner initially refuted it by reading "200, no redirect" and "404 with location" as different mechanisms; a debugger overturned that with header evidence showing they are one rule with a data-dependent status. Do not strike this note.

matchers.pattern: Expected: 308\s+Received: (200|404) on a path differing only by a trailing slash
manifest carries status 308 for the built-in normalizer vs 307 for config redirects

ocelhq-e8z.note: WIDENED in sweep-2026-07-27c: no longer trailing-slash-specific. On a fixture with NO trailingSlash anywhere, all four next.config.js redirects returned 200 carrying a byte-correct Location (correct :path* substitution and query string), each with x-amzn-requestid so throttling is ruled out. Rule loading and matching are FINE - only the status is never set to 3xx, and browsers ignore Location on a 200 so the user silently lands on the wrong page. Mechanism: result.redirect is never populated, so dispatch falls past index.ts:458 to resolvedPathname -> Lambda -> catch-all renders 200 while the rule's location is merged on at :390-392. NARROWED: middleware redirects WORK (307, answered in-worker, no x-amzn-*), and next.config.js REWRITES WORK (verified by body: /config-rewrite-before renders page_config-rewrite-after). So the rule pipeline applies rewrites but not redirect statuses. REFUTED: an earlier probe in this same sweep saw HTTP 522 on the itms-apps:// (with slashes) destination and hypothesised an external-scheme doFetch failure at index.ts:464-465; on a clean deployment it returns the same 200+location face as the other three. That 522 was teardown contamination - do not chase a separate external-scheme defect. Downstream partner remains ocelhq-xlj. Shared fix site: workers/nextjs/src/index.ts.

ocelhq-9q8.oneLine: Prerendered app-page RSC responses carry content-type text/html; client navigation degrades to a full page reload

matchers.pattern: RSC: 1 request answered with content-type text/html instead of text/x-component

matchers.check: Send `RSC: 1` (with or without ?_rsc=) to a prerendered app page. Confirmed sweep-2026-07-27c: body is correct flight data (starts `1:I[...]`, zero DOCTYPE occurrences) but content-type is text/html; charset=utf-8 instead of text/x-component, so the client router discards the prefetch and refetches.

Interception fixtures (interception-dynamic-segment, interception-dynamic-single-segment). The (.) route IS matched server-side (x-matched-path: /(.)<route>), but the RSC response is labelled text/html, so the client router aborts the soft navigation and hard-loads the URL; a document load carries no Next-Url, so no interception happens and @modal/[...catchAll] fills the slot.

matchers.pattern: page\.waitForSelector: Timeout \d+ms exceeded[\s\S]*waiting for locator\('#modal h3'\)
matchers.check: Same defect, other assertion face: the catch-all modal page renders no <h3>, so any '#modal h3' wait times out.

matchers.pattern: 200 + x-matched-path naming a `/(.)` interception route + content-type text/html on an RSC request
matchers.check: Never a 404 and never a routing bug. Curl the intercepted path with `RSC: 1` and `Next-Url: /`: x-matched-path shows the (.) route and the body is valid flight, only content-type is wrong. Interception routes that go x-nextjs-cache: MISS (Lambda-rendered, no build-time cache entry) return text/x-component and PASS - that pass/fail split is the fingerprint, not prerendered-vs-not.

router-autoscroll 'should scroll to top of document with new metadata' ONLY, and only when the received top equals the PREVIOUS page's scroll position exactly (unchanged, not partial). Confirm by curling the click target with `RSC: 1` + `Next-Router-State-Tree` (no Next-Router-Prefetch): if it answers text/html the router hard-reloads and scrollTop reads off the OLD document until the reload commits (~1.5-2.0s warm, x-ocel-cache: MISS), so a 3000ms retry window fails under load. Do NOT match a bare scroll-position mismatch: partial/animated scroll offsets, sticky/fixed/invisible-first-element cases and horizontal-scroll assertions are separate behaviours.

matchers.pattern: soft client navigation silently replaced by a full document load (all static chunks re-fetched) after a click on a next/link
matchers.check: Trace the click in a browser. If the non-prefetch RSC fetch returns text/html and is immediately followed by a plain document GET of the same path, it is this defect. Any assertion with a retry budget under ~3s that reads DOM/scroll/URL state during that window will see the OLD document's values unchanged.

A parallel-route @modal slot rendering default.tsx after a would-be soft nav. Confirm with: curl -D- <target> -H 'RSC: 1' -H 'Next-Url: <source>' returns content-type text/html and x-nextjs-prerender: 1.

Fires when the expected value was read from a window.* variable (e.g. window.__navStart) set BEFORE a next/link click. NaN means the variable no longer exists, i.e. the soft navigation became a full document load. Confirm: curl -D- -H "RSC: 1" <target> returns content-type text/html while adding -H "Next-Router-Prefetch: 1" returns text/x-component.

matchers.pattern: content-type: text/html with x-ocel-cache: MISS and x-amzn-requestid present on an `RSC: 1` request whose PREFETCH variant is text/x-component with x-ocel-cache: PRERENDER
matchers.check: The prefetch/non-prefetch content-type split on one URL is the fingerprint. The prefetch variant PASSING is what hides this defect from most navigation tests, so a fixture using prefetch={false} is the reliable repro.

matchers.pattern: .ocel/output/apps/<app>/cache/*.cache.json with value.headers content-type text/html and value.rscHeaders content-type text/x-component
matchers.check: STATIC confirmation, no deploy needed: the entry stores both variants and the Lambda cache-handler serves value.headers. Cheapest possible detection for future sweeps.

ocelhq-9q8.note: Confirmed on new evidence in sweep-2026-07-27c and now owns 3 tests across 2 suites (metadata added app-prefetch's 2 prefetch-reuse failures). The payload is RIGHT and only the label is wrong. SECOND OBSERVATION worth its own issue: every RSC request is x-ocel-cache: MISS with x-amzn-requestid present (invokes Lambda) while the equivalent HTML request is PRERENDER/HIT and never touches Lambda, despite cache-control: s-maxage=31536000. Every prefetch of a static page therefore costs an invocation, which interacts badly with ocelhq-9d3's quota of 10. sweep-2026-07-27e: also owns all 9 failures in interception-dynamic-segment. Those look like an interception/route-selection defect (modal slot resolves to @modal/[...catchAll]) but are purely downstream of this content-type: the worker/Lambda select the (.) route correctly. Ruled out vs ocelhq-hzp (these are 200s, and Next-Router-State-Tree + RSC:1 on this preview returned 200, not 500) and vs ocelhq-dan (no action redirect, no per-route-split involvement). sweep-2026-07-27e: ALSO owns router-autoscroll 'should scroll to top of document with new metadata'. Reproduced live on e2e-stg-534df07b: the click's non-prefetch RSC fetch returns text/html, the router hard-reloads, and document.documentElement.scrollTop keeps reading the OLD page's 8388 until the reload commits at ~1500ms - the earlier rebuttal ('a hard load would land at top:0 so it would PASS') was wrong about the interval, not the endpoint. Metadata is a red herring: the passing control /hoisted takes the identical hard-reload path and passes only because its reload lands inside the 3000ms retry budget. Refuted en route: the __NEXT_EXPERIMENTAL_APP_NEW_SCROLL_HANDLER harness-gap theory (the failing test is ungated, predates the flag via next.js f8afd611df / #74748, and upstream CI runs the suite with the flag set to false); also ruled out ocelhq-wiw (head-rewrite, different path - the delivered <head> here is correct) and ocelhq-14y (no fetches, no revalidate in the fixture). sweep-2026-07-27g: gained 2 more suites (static-rsc-cache-components, metadata-static-file-intercepting-route), both confirmed at HTTP level. NEW MECHANISM DETAIL: the build-time cache entry stores BOTH variants — value.headers -> text/html and value.rscHeaders -> text/x-component — and the Lambda cache-handler replays the wrong one, so the prefetch path is correct while the non-prefetch path is broken. Also NOT confined to plain prerenders: the static-rsc-cache-components fixture uses cacheComponents: true with a 'use cache' page. In the intercepting-route case the hard nav lands on a DIFFERENT route tree, so interception is lost entirely and the suite reports "missing metadata" when the real failure is "the intercepted route was never rendered".
ocelhq-9q8.notes: Also the cause of interception-dynamic-single-segment 'should intercept with purely static multi-segment paths' (modal reads 'default'): the degraded hard reload drops next-url, so the @modal slot falls to default.tsx. Only interception targets with dispatch kind: prerender are affected; kind: lambda interception routes serve text/x-component correctly. Sibling failure in that suite is ocelhq-4fg, not this.

ocelhq-4lw.oneLine: Edge bundle drops Next's wasm binding names, so every next/og edge route 500s with 'Edge invocation failed'
ocelhq-4lw.fixSite: next-adapter.mts:501 (carry a wasmBindings map) + renderEdgeShim :392-419 (assign globals)

ocelhq-4lw.note: Next's middleware-manifest.json gives each edge wasm as {name, filePath} and the NAME is load-bearing - the Turbopack chunk resolves wasm via a bare GLOBAL of that name. next-adapter.mts:501 destructures only { modules: wasmModules } from moduleIds, discarding idByKey - the exact opposite of :496, which keeps it for chunks. ocelhq-dc4.oneLine: Dynamic route params always empty for runtime='edge' routes; worker never injects Next's nxtP query params
ocelhq-dc4.fixSite: workers/nextjs/src/index.ts:493-501 (the edge branch, NOT originUrl's shared body)

matchers.check: Route has `export const runtime = 'edge'` and a dynamic/catch-all segment. Live request returns 200 with x-matched-path showing the bracketed route (e.g. /edge/[[...slug]]) but an empty params object. Not a 500 and not 'Edge invocation failed' - that is ocelhq-4lw.

ocelhq-dc4.note: An edge entry is a single-route bundle and cannot re-match a pathname, so the invoker must inject dynamic params as nxtP-prefixed query entries. edge-route-module-wrapper.ts:106-109 derives params SOLELY from request.nextUrl.searchParams, and NEXT_QUERY_PARAM_PREFIX='nxtP' (constants.ts:6) is PRODUCED by Next's own build adapter at build/adapter/build-complete.ts:1727,1755,1759 - so the deployment layer is contractually expected to populate them, this is not an optional convention. originUrl (index.ts:718-721) forwards the pathname plus the ORIGINAL search string and injects nothing. EDGE-ONLY: case 'lambda' (:484-488) forwards to a full route module whose prepare() re-matches params (route-module.ts:808-822, fallback :940-949). DISTINCT from ocelhq-bvm despite both citing :718-721 - bvm ENCODES a path already forwarded and its fix belongs inside originUrl's shared body, whereas this one must NOT go there because lambda and prerender callers must keep forwarding the untouched search string. Fails as WRONG DATA AT 200, which per ocelhq-9d3's history is the more dangerous mode.

ocelhq-kpd.oneLine: No /_next/image optimizer: every next/image src 404s (worker finds no route, falls through to the 404 asset)

matchers.check: Any request to /_next/image returning 404. The adapter emits no dispatch entry for this path, so it is unconditional.

Attribute here ONLY if the fetched URL is /_next/image. A bare 200-vs-404 matches ocelhq-e8z, ocelhq-xlj and ocelhq-iud too. Confirm the response carries NO x-matched-path AND NO x-ocel-cache AND NO x-amzn-requestid - present headers mean the request DID reach a handler and this is not the cause.

ocelhq-kpd.note: UNBUILT FEATURE, not a regression - filed as a bug because the gap is unacknowledged and fails silently. The adapter never reads Next's images config at all (images|imageSizes|deviceSizes|remotePatterns|unoptimized|imagesManifest return zero hits across worker, lambda-entrypoints and next-runtime), and the emitter's dispatch map has exactly four kinds - lambda, edge, static, prerender - so no image entry is possible BY CONSTRUCTION. ocelhq-94l's milestones do not include image optimization and there is no acknowledgement in CONTEXT.md, docs/adr/ or package READMEs. DO NOT attribute the whole app-dir/next-image suite here - it is TWO defects; the 5 ssr/browser tests are ocelhq-68p. Confounder CLEARED in a follow-up probe: /_next/static/media/*.png|jpg serve correctly (200, image/png/jpeg, valid magic bytes, x-matched-path present), so the wave-4 static-media 404s were teardown contamination and the passthrough interim is VIABLE. Recommended: (1) unoptimized-style passthrough - and it MUST validate against localPatterns/remotePatterns or it becomes an open SSRF proxy; (2) independently, warn at build when next/image is used with no optimizer. Blast radius: 60 test/e2e suite dirs use next/image or next/legacy/image; next-image-new/unoptimized is a useful control that should pass today.

ocelhq-a9x.oneLine: __NEXT_TEST_MODE never set for custom-script deploys: no fetch-priority header, and every next.browser() burns a flat 10s hydration timeout
ocelhq-a9x.fixSite: scripts/e2e-next/deploy.mjs:152-157 (add NEXT_PRIVATE_TEST_MODE=e2e to the spawnSync env)

matchers.check: Any assertion on next-test-fetch-priority is unsatisfiable until NEXT_PRIVATE_TEST_MODE=e2e reaches the build. Never an adapter defect.

grep 'Waiting hydration|Hydration complete' in the run log and diff the timestamps. Exactly 10.0s means next-webdriver.ts:188 hit its setTimeout fallback and hydration was NEVER detected. Present in 196/202 page loads across sweeps a, b and c.

matchers.pattern: request\.allHeaders: Target page, context or browser has been closed
matchers.check: Cascade, not a defect. Compare the reported source line against the ENCLOSING test: a page.on('request') handler line belonging to the PREVIOUS test means Jest mis-attributed a late unhandled rejection.

ocelhq-a9x.note: Harness/tooling, not adapter. deployUsingCustomScript (next-deploy.ts:47, env :53-58) passes only {...process.env, NEXT_TEST_DIR, ...this.env}; the Vercel path injects --build-env NEXT_PRIVATE_TEST_MODE=e2e (:446) and the local path injects __NEXT_TEST_MODE (base.ts:673) - the custom-script path injects NEITHER. Consequences: (1) fetch-server-response.ts:689 never emits next-test-fetch-priority; (2) window.__NEXT_HYDRATED never fires (client/index.tsx:601, app-index.tsx:318), so next-webdriver.ts:188 hits its hard 10s fallback on EVERY page load. Measured: 202 waits, 1967s (32.8 min) across sweeps a/b/c, 196 of them exactly 10.00s; __NEXT_HYDRATED_CB has NEVER fired in any sweep. CORRECTNESS RULING (conservative): the flag does not disable hydration, only the SIGNAL, so this is a race, not a systematic wrong answer - NO existing finding is plausibly an artifact, since hzp, 9q8, 7og, xlj, e7w and sae all rest on curl-reproducible HTTP evidence. The real cost is that green BROWSER results are weaker evidence than assumed (negative assertions can pass vacuously). Fix chain verified end to end: deploy.mjs env -> spawnSync -> ocel build -> next build -> loadConfig runs the shim at base.ts:470-478 -> sets __NEXT_TEST_MODE -> define-env.ts:269 inlines it. Use NEXT_PRIVATE_TEST_MODE, not __NEXT_TEST_MODE directly. Also: test/e2e/instrumentation-client-hook and app-dir/instant-navigation-testing-api read window.__NEXT_HYDRATED directly and would fail outright in deploy mode.

ocelhq-68p.oneLine: logs.mjs omits NEXT_SUPPORTS_IMMUTABLE_ASSETS, so the harness demands a &dpl= token Ocel never stamps

ocelhq-68p.note: Harness-contract defect in scripts/e2e-next, NOT an adapter bug - Ocel's assets ARE content-hashed, so carrying no dpl= token is correct and arguably better than what the harness assumes. The `0` comes from the harness's own injected post-build script at base.ts:320 (chained :329), evaluating (VERCEL_IMMUTABLE_STATIC_FILES_ENABLED && NEXT_ENABLE_ADAPTER==='1') ? 1 : 0 - false because we are not on Vercel, NOT because config.deploymentId is unset. THE CRUX: repo-wide grep for IMMUTABLE_ASSET_TOKEN across all of Next.js returns exactly ONE hit and it is a COMMENT, so the opt-out lib.mjs:144-146 documents does not exist and lib.mjs:151 is inert. FIX (a): emit NEXT_SUPPORTS_IMMUTABLE_ASSETS: 1 from logs.mjs ahead of the replayed build log - this states the TRUTH about the deployment and has zero runtime effect. Fix (b) (set config.deploymentId) REJECTED: it makes the test pass by degrading the product, rotating every asset's CDN cache key on every deploy - precisely the cost content-hashing exists to avoid. Caveats: the marker is honoured only under IS_TURBOPACK_TEST (next-deploy.ts:43-45), so (a) silently no-ops on webpack; and (a) does NOT fix next-image-legacy/default, because getDeploymentIdQuery (base.ts:865-868) never consults supportsImmutableAssets - that suite needs a manifest exclusion (note its sibling base-path already carries skipDeployment with a comment about this exact problem). Blast radius: app-dir/next-image, app-dir/worker, next-image-legacy/default. No prior misattribution: zero dpl= occurrences in either archived sweep. Sibling harness defects: ocelhq-a9x, ocelhq-7gk.

Confirm by fetching the same file under the basePath instead: if that returns 200 text/javascript while the assetPrefix form 404s, it is this issue. A 404 carrying x-matched-path pointing at the basePath-rewritten path is decisive — it proves the rewrite matched and the STATIC LOOKUP missed, which is what distinguishes this from a routing/dispatch gap.

ocelhq-34gs.notes: Do NOT attribute to ocelhq-zpu: zpu's own test ('rewrites that do not start with assetPrefix should still work') PASSED in sweep-2026-07-27e, so that run was a non-reproduction of zpu. Do NOT attribute to ocelhq-kpd: its 200/404 matcher is scoped to /_next/image. Masking hazard: browser tests in the same suite still PASS with every bundle 404ing, because the hydration check short-circuits ('Not a next.js page, resolving hydrate check') — see ocelhq-a9x.

ocelhq-k8pr.title: site root / 404s when pages/index.tsx is auto-static-optimized — dispatch key is /index

matchers.check: Attribute ONLY if the 404 is on the site ROOT '/' AND the app has a pages/index.tsx with no getStaticProps/getServerSideProps (auto-static-optimized). Decisive control: if the same fixture family has an 'optional catch-all' variant where '/' is served by pages/[[...slug]].tsx (getServerSideProps) and that variant PASSES the identical tests, it is this issue.

matchers.pattern: warmUpRoute(next, '/') exhausts its retries, then the browser loads '/' and logs a 404 resource error before hydrating the 404 page

ocelhq-k8pr.notes: SIBLING of ocelhq-e7w, not a duplicate, and e7w's fix will NOT fix this. e7w is the FILE NAME (static/<route> missing .html); this is the DISPATCH KEY ('/index' vs '/'). None of e7w's three specific matchers fire here — no 'Download is starting', no application/octet-stream, no EEXIST/EISDIR; the build succeeds. Same family as ocelhq-iud (route stored under its on-disk key rather than its runtime path).

ocelhq-l2ef.title: pages-router _next/data navigation to a nested dynamic SSR route gets empty params

matchers.pattern: pages-router client navigation renders the CORRECT component at the CORRECT URL, but getServerSideProps receives params = {} (all params undefined) on the /_next/data/<buildId>/... request
matchers.check: Confirm the same route loaded as a full DOCUMENT returns correct params — if the document path works and only the _next/data path has empty params, it is this issue.

ocelhq-l2ef.notes: Shares the 'params always empty' SHAPE with ocelhq-dc4 but is NOT the same: dc4 is scoped to runtime='edge' app routes; this is a nodejs Lambda on the pages router. Do not merge on symptom shape alone. They may share a param-propagation seam.

ocelhq-ktl.title: harness: sweep never sets NEXT_ENABLE_ADAPTER=1, silently skipping 8 adapter-gated suites

matchers.pattern: Jest reports a suite as '<n> skipped, 1 passed' where the single pass is the synthetic 'should skip next deploy' case, AND the suite sets skipDeployment: !isAdapterTest

ocelhq-ktl.notes: NOT an adapter defect — a harness configuration gap present in every sweep a..e. Affected: partial-fallback-shell-upgrade, partial-fallback-root-blocking, cache-components-prerender-matrix, sub-shell-generation, sub-shell-generation-middleware (app-dir), plus i18n-api-support, not-found-with-pages-i18n, middleware-rewrites. Setting the var is safe: the other NEXT_ENABLE_ADAPTER consumers in next-deploy.ts live in the Vercel CLI branch, which the custom-deploy-script path short-circuits past at line 48. Check ocelhq-68p afterwards (base.ts:320 gates NEXT_SUPPORTS_IMMUTABLE_ASSETS on the same var).

ocelhq-slzm.oneLine: Server action result arrives correct but LATE — cold per-route Lambda start pushes it past the test retry budget

matchers.check: Correlate the click timestamp in the jest log with INIT_START/START/END in the route Lambda's CloudWatch group. If the handler ran and END lands after click+3000ms with a 200 text/x-component body, it is this issue — NOT a broken action.

ocelhq-slzm.note: Discovered sweep-2026-07-27g, merging two clusters that looked like separate action bugs. The action is not broken, it is late. Warm curl returns 200 text/x-component, x-amzn-requestid present, x-ocel-cache: BYPASS, body 1:"result". CloudWatch shows exactly ONE successful invocation per action: cache-components click 21:14:40.058 -> INIT_START 21:14:42.087 (2.03s pre-Lambda latency) -> END 21:14:43.805, i.e. 0.75s past retry()'s 3000ms budget; navigation-with-queued-actions ended ~0.3s past budget. Routing is correct (kind prerender with bypassFor next-action; dispatchPrerender bypasses cache for any non-GET). The per-route Lambda split is the upstream cause: every action route meets a cold function. Silent failure mode — a well-formed RSC payload arrives after the assertion gave up, so the UI shows a stale value rather than an error.
ocelhq-slzm.notes: Ruled DISTINCT from ocelhq-9d3 (no 502 during either failing run), ocelhq-dan (no redirect, no request-count assertion; per-route split is upstream not identical) and ocelhq-81a (here the response is correct and does arrive). NOTE flagged on ocelhq-81a: its log shape (six 500ms retries, no error) matches this cluster and 81a may itself be a late-response case rather than a no-navigation case.

ocelhq-2f8x.oneLine: Server action redirect() 500s on every runtime='edge' route — requestMeta.initURL is always undefined in the edge shim

matchers.pattern: edge-dispatched route: POST with next-action returns 500 with x-edge-runtime: 1, content-type text/x-component and a flight body containing E{"digest", while the same action id on a nodejs route returns 303 + x-action-redirect
a suite whose nodejs variant passes while the runtime='edge' variant of the same fixture times out
matchers.check: curl -sS -o /dev/null -D - -X POST "$URL/<edge-route>" -H "next-action: $ID" -F '1_$ACTION_ID_'"$ID"'=' | grep -i 'HTTP/2 500\|x-edge-runtime'

ocelhq-2f8x.note: Discovered sweep-2026-07-27g. Same action id returns 303 + x-action-redirect: /redirect;push + x-amzn-requestid on /server-action/node, but 500 with x-edge-runtime: 1, no x-action-redirect and body 1:E{"digest":"676858681"} on /server-action/edge. The edge route IS emitted and HEALTHY: dispatch[/server-action/edge] = {kind:edge, entryKey:middleware_app/server-action/edge/page}; GET, non-action POST and RSC POST all 200; a bogus next-action id 404s with x-nextjs-action-not-found: 1, so the action is found and runs. Middleware is incidental — bypassing it via x-prerender-revalidate reproduces the identical 500. ROOT CAUSE: the edge bundle's shim invokes handler(request, { ..., requestMeta: {} }) and edge-ssr-app.ts forwards that verbatim, so getRequestMeta(req,'initURL') is always undefined on edge; action-handler.ts:400-418 then throws InvariantError('Missing initURL') on the redirect path (no __NEXT_PRIVATE_ORIGIN in bundle.json env). The nodejs path is saved by the node-only back-fill at route-module.ts:694-700.
ocelhq-2f8x.notes: Ruled DISTINCT from ocelhq-dc4 (same 'empty edge invocation context' FAMILY but a different missing input — params via nextUrl.searchParams vs origin via requestMeta.initURL; neither fix resolves the other), ocelhq-4lw (4lw throws on chunk evaluation and yields the worker's 22-byte 'Edge invocation failed'; here the bundle evaluates and bundle.json wasm is []), ocelhq-81a and ocelhq-dan. DOC FINDING: the repo README claim that the adapter 'emits nodejs functions only and skips edge routes' is STALE — edge routes ARE emitted and dispatch as kind:edge.

ocelhq-qcpc.oneLine: server action redirect() to a RELATIVE URL produces no client navigation; absolute URL to the same target works

matchers.pattern: waiting for locator\('#redirected'\) to be visible
a server action redirect() given a relative path leaves the browser on the action page, while the absolute-URL variant of the same action navigates
matchers.check: Confirm the origin returns 303 with a RELATIVE x-action-redirect value. If x-action-redirect is absolute, this is not qcpc.

ocelhq-qcpc.note: Runtime-independent (fails on both nodejs and edge), which refutes ocelhq-2f8x. Distinct from ocelhq-dan, which fails only AFTER a successful navigation on toHaveLength(1)/received 2. Check whether ocelhq-81a collapses into this.

ocelhq-r6ul.oneLine: first/early server-action POST intermittently gets a Cloudflare 502 with no x-amzn-* headers (non-throttle half of the closed ocelhq-9d3)

matchers.pattern: 502 with server: cloudflare and retry-after: 60 and NO x-amzn-* header of any kind, on a POST carrying next-action

matchers.check: Confirm absence of x-amzn-requestid before attributing. Quota is 1000, so this is NOT throttling; sweep-f/g CloudWatch shows the Lambda IS invoked, implicating the worker->Function-URL response leg.

ocelhq-r6ul.note: Inherited from ocelhq-9d3. Trigger UNKNOWN: a deliberate 75s idle gap did not reproduce it. Distinct from ocelhq-slzm (late but correct 200).

suiteCounts.note: grep -c skipDeployment over test/e2e/app-dir/*/*.test.ts. 190 of 508 app-dir suites (37%) set skipDeployment:true, so under NEXT_TEST_MODE=deploy the harness replaces the suite body with a synthetic `should skip next deploy` case and no adapter signal is obtainable. Coverage percentages against 690 therefore overstate reachable coverage. Check this flag BEFORE spending a wave slot - two slots were lost to it in sweep-2026-07-27b. ADDITION from sweep-2026-07-27c: skipDeployment is not the only structural trap. A suite can also bail at DESCRIBE SCOPE on `if ((global as any).isNextDeploy)`, substituting a single no-op case - rewrites-redirects does exactly this and cost a wave slot. Inventory `grep -l isNextDeploy` alongside skipDeployment before composing a wave.

baselineManifest.note: The file contains literally {} - no baseline has ever been recorded. The README promotion rule ("delete the case line when a fix makes it pass") has nothing to act on, and NEXT_EXTERNAL_TESTS_FILTERS is not set by the sweep runner command anyway. The `known` bucket in these sweeps therefore derives entirely from Next.js upstream test/deploy-tests-manifest.json, which this repo does not own. Recording drift against it is informational only.
